Synopsis:
A retrospective assessment of Meloni's government — now Italy's longest-serving administration — covering its key legislative agenda. Major reforms (judiciary overhaul, direct PM election, regional autonomy) have largely stalled or been struck down. Migration policy delivered partial results, with the Albania detention scheme underperforming its mandate. Security legislation has been the most active and successful area. Tax reform was modest with negligible net impact on the overall tax burden. Welfare tightened via replacement of Citizens' Income.
